HardwareState: Statistics bitstream camera720_calibrated_stats_delay_top is currently in volatile SRAM; no new programming or native EDA was performed for this report.

TransportAndModeFacts.Limits: Arithmetic envelope only. Excludes line/frame blanking, exposure extension, admission/bank stalls and hardware timing. Core processing and accepted-frame statistics cannot alone measure all sensor frames.

Interpretation.StrongestCurrentFinding: Across 119 valid 1-second windows, source accepted, processed, and unique presented counters all advanced by 15 per nominal second with no rejected packets or identity mismatches. No observed counter gap proves a downstream drop at this cadence.
Interpretation.MostLikelyFirstHypothesis: The 15 FPS cadence is set by sensor/mode timing or an admission cadence. The nominal 42 MHz/14.999 FPS sequence model is numerically consistent with the measured 15 FPS, but the actual PCLK and sensor-good cadence were not measured, so this remains a hypothesis.
Interpretation.NotProven: The current evidence cannot distinguish sensor pacing from display-bank waiting or a processing scheduler that happens to sustain exactly 15 FPS, because the bitstream does not export PCLK edges, sensor good/bad, DMA-complete, pending wait, display-grant wait, cache miss/fill or process-cycle counters.

ProcessingModelLimits.Limits: Same-fill-count structural estimate only; no optimized run, preserved miss count, RAM inference, actual FPS benefit, or per-frame distribution is proven.

DecisionTree.Condition: PCLK edge/good-frame cadence is approximately 15 FPS and DMA-complete/source-accepted match it; downstream counters remain equal.
DecisionTree.Conclusion: Input sensor/mode cadence is the limiting stage.
DecisionTree.Action: Use a separately audited 720p30 sensor configuration candidate; do not change correction math first.

DecisionTree.Condition: Good frames exceed source-accepted frames, or accepted frames exceed processed/unique output, or pending/display-grant wait dominates.
DecisionTree.Conclusion: Admission, bank ownership, display scheduling, or output cadence is limiting.
DecisionTree.Action: Instrument and optimize lease/pending/display scheduling while preserving the two-bank/CRC contract.

DecisionTree.Condition: Accepted and processed counts diverge, process cycles approach the inter-frame interval, or cache miss/scatter counters dominate.
DecisionTree.Action: First evaluate the isolated 32-to-16 scatter-cycle packing experiment at unchanged logical capacity, then repeat correctness, physical timing, and FPS checks.

MinimumNextCandidate.Name: 720p input-cadence diagnostic plus isolated 720p30 sensor-mode branch
MinimumNextCandidate.Phase1: Keep correction RTL and current bank/DDR contracts unchanged. Add read-only counters to the existing UART packet for PCLK edges per reference window, sensor good/bad frames, last line bytes/lines, DMA-complete, source-accepted, processed, unique-presented, pending/display-grant wait, no-grant, overflow/underflow and process-cycle min/max.
MinimumNextCandidate.Phase2IfSensorLimited: Prepare an isolated OV5640 1280x720 RGB565 30-FPS register candidate (the source model references an 84 MHz PCLK branch) with explicit readback, measured PCLK, exact 2560 active bytes x 720 lines, frame freshness, new input constraints and full native timing/CDC/IO audit. Do not overwrite the 15-FPS bitstream.
MinimumNextCandidate.Phase2IfComputeLimited: Prepare an isolated cache/scatter candidate only after counters show cache/compute pressure; preserve logical block size, bank protocol, CRC and output contract.
MinimumNextCandidate.Acceptance: At least 120 seconds per candidate, matching build/profile IDs, no packet loss or identity mismatch, independent PCLK/reference measurement or explicit limitation, zero underflow/overflow/CRC faults, and source/processed/unique rates reported separately.

Limits: UART uses nominal 125 MHz ticks and assumes continuous reset epoch within each window.
No independent PCLK, sensor exposure cadence, HDMI refresh, underflow or fault-status measurement is present.
The 42 MHz/14.999 FPS sequence is a model, not a board measurement.
The two-frame RTL trace and scatter estimate are simulation/model evidence, not a hardware throughput measurement.
